title: The hook writes every trailer a commit carries

statements.says: No model types a trailer the loop relies on.
Claude Code's own commit credit is always off.
The Plugin's PreToolUse hook adds each trailer with git commit --trailer, which git always puts in the message's trailer block.
The hook adds a Skillworks-Session trailer on every commit.
The hook adds a Ticket trailer on a loop Session's commits, with the value the driver hands that Session.
The hook adds Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com> when co-authored-by in docs/agents/loop.json says show.
Pull requests keep Claude Code's own credit, set from the same co-authored-by answer.
The hook keeps each commit's own text word for word and adds only --trailer arguments after it.
How git settles a trailer the message already holds lives in the repo's local git config: addIfDifferent for Skillworks-Session and Co-Authored-By, and replace for Ticket.
Before each commit it rewrites, the hook writes the three trailer rules with git config --local in the repo at the Session's cwd, when one is missing or holds another value.
The hook writes the Plugin's trailer rule over a team's own.
A locked git config gets 3 more tries, 200 ms apart.
When the config write still fails, or cwd is no repo, the commit goes on with its trailers and without the rules.
The hook never answers "allow", so the team's own permission rules decide each commit.
The hook refuses a commit with a credit line the model typed, giving its reason, and the Session runs it again without the line.
The hook replaces a Ticket line the model typed.
A hand run types its own Ticket line.
The finish step still checks that git reads the Ticket trailer, so a commit the hook never saw, such as one made through a git alias, is mended before Land.
A repo with no co-authored-by key keeps whatever credit Claude Code gives it.
A credit line typed in a message file a commit reads with -F is not refused, because the hook cannot read that file.
A clone's .git/config gains three lines on the first commit the hook rewrites there, and setup writes nothing for them.
The addIfDifferent rule never removes or changes a person's Co-Authored-By line.
A commit made before the trailer rules are written falls back on git's own rule, and the ticket-trailer check in finish stays the net for a Ticket that went wrong.

Models wrote the Co-Authored-By line as a paragraph of its own, and git reads trailers only from the last paragraph, so the Ticket line above it became body text and Land refused the commit after its Session had gone.
The docs already said where a trailer goes, and the models broke the rule anyway.
Adding only --trailer arguments after the commit's own text means an allow rule the command matched still matches.
The repo's local git config is shared by every worktree of a clone.
A fixed credit line is always true, and the Session trailer leads to the exact model.
Replace is safe for Ticket because a loop Session works on one ticket.
A repo with no co-authored-by key chose nothing, so it keeps Claude Code's credit.
A hand run can type its own Ticket line because the credit instruction that stranded it is gone.
Keeping Claude Code's credit and letting the hook add only Ticket was rejected, because the model would still type a trailer, and a typed trailer is what went wrong.
Naming the model in the credit, as Claude Code does, was rejected, because the PreToolUse hook is not told the model and a Session can switch models or hand work to a sub-agent on another one.
Removing a credit line the model typed was rejected, because the line sits inside shell quoting and an edit there can break the message or the command.
Letting git's replace rule settle a second credit line was rejected, because it deletes the nearest Co-Authored-By line, which can be a person's.
Handing a hand run's Session its ticket through a command was rejected, because the model would still have to remember to run the command.

Putting the trailer rules before commit, as git -c trailer.<key>.ifExists=... commit, was rejected, because git -c k=v commit does not match the allow rule Bash(git commit:*), so every loop commit in acceptEdits mode asked for an approval nobody gave.

Putting the trailer rules in the env block of .claude/settings.json as GIT_CONFIG_COUNT and its pairs was rejected, because a loop Session cannot write under .claude/ and GIT_CONFIG_COUNT can clash with a team's own.
Having the hook answer "allow" for the commit it rewrites was rejected, because an allow skips the team's own ask rules and the hook has no call to overrule them.
